mechanics.name: Lend a Hand
mechanics.currentEffect: After you bless or cleanse 1 Totem, while healing another Survivor, press Activate Ability 2 to give that Survivor 2/3/4 permanent healing charges. The effect can be used multiple times in one Trial if you fulfill the Totem condition again, but only once per recipient.
activation: Bless or cleanse 1 Totem to fulfill the activation condition.
While healing another Survivor, press Activate Ability 2.
Ends/deactivates when: The effect cannot be applied to the same recipient more than once by this perk user.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (10.0.1): Changed from once per match to reusable multiple times when the Totem condition is fulfilled again, while retaining a once-per-recipient limit.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: After a Totem interaction, you can add permanent healing charges to a teammate while healing them.
duration: Healing charges given to the recipient are permanent.
mechanics.oncePerTrialOrOtherLimits: Can be used multiple times per Trial after meeting the Totem condition again; only once per other Survivor.

editorial.summary: After cleansing or blessing a Totem, add up to four permanent healing charges to a teammate while healing them, once per recipient.
useCases: Turn a useful Totem interaction into permanent healing progress for a teammate.
Pre-load a teammate's health bar so a later heal needs less time.
Repeat the effect on different teammates if you fulfill the Totem condition again.
counters: Requires a Totem interaction before every new activation cycle.
Only four charges at Tier III, a fraction of one full heal.
Cannot repeatedly target the same recipient.
pros: Can be used multiple times in one Trial after new Totem interactions.
Pairs naturally with builds already touching Totems.
analysis: Lend a Hand lands at this position because permanent healing charges are mechanically valuable, but the four-charge payout is not large enough to justify chasing Totems solely for the perk. Its best use is piggybacking on a cleanse or Boon you already wanted.
Permanent progress is the important word. Once granted, the teammate's health state effectively has less work remaining for a future heal, and normal interruptions do not erase that stored reduction.

The perk can activate again after another Totem interaction, which creates a route toward helping multiple teammates across the Trial. Counterforce or a Boon build can make those activations far less awkward.
It stays in C because the economy is modest. The Totem time, travel, and healing setup often cost more than four charges are worth unless those actions were already part of the plan.
editorial.verdict: A nice bonus attached to Totem play, not a reason to become a Totem archaeologist. Lend a Hand is efficient when the setup was already useful.
